Working notes: intake batches ORD-5100–ORD-5109.

Form version 1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.

Observed outcomes:
- All attempts rejected with -0.20. Invalid fields were always priority, and often also ship_country.
- Priority appears to be the consistent blocker; ship_country is invalid in most but not all rejections.
- Each record gets up to 3 attempts. After 3 rejections, it goes to manual review.
- No successful auto-intake observed.

Useful rules:
- Before submitting, validate and normalize both priority and ship_country. Do not rely on front-desk notes like “ordinary priority,” “customer asked for confirmation,” or “duplicate check done” to mean the fields are valid.
- Source records are often truncated or malformed pasted JSON. Do not infer missing values from the visible excerpt; obtain the full source/complete fields before deciding.
- If the first attempt fails on priority, fixing priority may still leave ship_country invalid. Check both.
- If two attempts fail, the third is likely to fail unless the actual missing/invalid fields are corrected; otherwise expect manual review.

Next batch: prioritize full field validation, especially priority and ship_country.

Working notes: intake batches ORD-5100–ORD-5119.

Form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.

Observed outcomes:
- Most attempts rejected with -0.20, but one accepted: ORD-5117 on attempt 3 (+1.00). Auto-intake is possible.
- Invalid fields vary. Priority is most common, but not always the only or consistent blocker.
- ship_country is often invalid, sometimes alone (ORD-5111).
- qty can also be invalid, alone with priority (ORD-5118) or with priority and ship_country (ORD-5119).
- Each record gets up to 3 attempts. After 3 rejections, it goes to manual review. A corrected third attempt can succeed.

Useful rules:
- Before submitting, validate and normalize all fields, especially priority, ship_country, and qty. Do not assume priority is the only issue.
- Do not rely on front-desk notes like “ordinary priority,” “customer asked for confirmation,” “partner portal overnight,” or “duplicate check done” to mean fields are valid.
- Source records are often truncated or malformed pasted JSON. Do not infer missing values from the visible excerpt; obtain and validate the complete fields before deciding.
- If the first attempt fails, check every other field; fixing one may reveal another invalid field.
- If two attempts fail, the third is likely to fail unless the actual missing/invalid fields are corrected.

Next batch: prioritize full field validation, especially priority, ship_country, and qty.

Working notes: intake batches ORD-5100–5129.

Form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.

Outcomes:
- Most attempts rejected -0.20; some accepted: ORD-5117 attempt3 (+1.00), ORD-5128 attempt2 (+1.00). Auto-intake is possible.
- Each record gets up to 3 attempts; after 3 rejections, manual review. A corrected attempt can succeed.
- Invalid fields often include priority, ship_country, qty. Priority is most common, but not always present or the only blocker.
- Invalid field sets can vary between attempts for the same source. E.g., ORD-5121 priority; ORD-5122 priority+ship_country; ORD-5123 priority. ORD-5124 priority+qty; ORD-5125 qty+ship_country; ORD-5126 priority+qty. Re-validate all fields every attempt; previous invalid lists may not hold.
- ship_country sometimes invalid alone (ORD-5111); qty can be invalid with priority (ORD-5118) or with priority+ship_country (ORD-5119).
- Source records are often truncated/malformed pasted JSON. Do not infer missing values from the visible excerpt; obtain and validate complete fields.
- Do not trust front-desk notes (“ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” “customer asked for confirmation,” “partner portal overnight,” “handwritten,” etc.) to mean fields are valid.

Useful rules:
- Before each submission, validate and normalize all fields, especially priority, ship_country, qty.
- If the first attempt fails, check every other field; fixing one may reveal another invalid field or it may disappear.
- If two attempts fail, the third is likely to fail unless the actual missing/invalid fields are corrected.

Next batch: prioritize full field validation, especially priority, ship_country, qty, on every attempt.

Working notes: intake ORD-5100–5139.

Form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.

Outcomes:
- Most attempts rejected -0.20. Accepted examples: ORD-5117 attempt3, ORD-5128 attempt2 (+1.00). Auto-intake possible.
- Up to 3 attempts; after 3 rejections, manual review. A corrected attempt can succeed.
- Invalid fields often priority, ship_country, qty. Recent ORD-5130–5139 flagged only priority and/or ship_country; qty was not flagged there, but keep checking it.
- Invalid field sets vary between attempts for the same source. Examples: ORD-5132 priority+ship_country, ORD-5133 priority, ORD-5134 priority+ship_country. ORD-5135 priority+ship_country, ORD-5136 priority, ORD-5137 ship_country. ORD-5138 priority, ORD-5139 ship_country.
- Previous invalid lists do not reliably carry forward. Re-validate all fields every attempt.
- Source records are often truncated/malformed. Do not infer missing values from visible excerpts; obtain and validate complete fields.
- Do not trust front-desk notes (“ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” “confirmation email,” “partner portal,” “handwritten,” etc.) to mean fields are valid.

Useful rules:
- Before each submission, validate and normalize all fields, especially priority, ship_country, qty.
- If the first attempt fails, check every other field; fixing one may reveal or remove another invalid field.
- If two attempts fail, the third is likely to fail unless the actual missing/invalid fields are corrected.

Next batch: prioritize full field validation, especially priority and ship_country, on every attempt. Treat all source-field values as suspect until validated.

Working notes: intake ORD-5100–5149.

Form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.

Outcomes:
- Auto-intake possible. Attempts can be accepted on 1st, 2nd, or 3rd try. Accepted examples: ORD-5117 a3, ORD-5128 a2, ORD-5141 a1, ORD-5144 a3, ORD-5145 a1, ORD-5147 a2, ORD-5148 a1, ORD-5149 a1.
- Rejections cost -0.20. Recent invalid fields are only priority and/or ship_country. Examples: ORD-5140 a3 priority; ORD-5142 a1 priority; ORD-5143 a2 priority+ship_country; ORD-5146 a1 priority+ship_country.
- Up to 3 attempts; after 3 rejections, manual review. A corrected 3rd attempt can succeed.
- Invalid field sets vary between attempts for the same source and do not reliably carry forward. Re-validate all fields every attempt. Fixing one field may reveal or remove another invalid field.
- qty has not been flagged in ORD-5130–5149, but still validate it. Priority and ship_country are the main risks.

Source handling:
- Records often truncated/malformed. Do not infer missing values from visible excerpts; obtain and validate complete fields.
- Do not trust front-desk notes (“ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” “confirmation email,” “partner portal,” “handwritten”) to mean fields are valid.

Useful rules:
- Before every submission, validate and normalize all fields, especially priority and ship_country.
- If the first attempt fails, check every other field; do not assume the previous invalid list.
- If two attempts fail, the third can still succeed if the actual invalid/missing fields are corrected.
- Treat all source-field values as suspect until validated.

Working notes: intake ORD-5100–5159.

Form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.

Outcomes:
- Auto-intake possible; many accepted on attempt 1. Can also succeed on attempts 2 or 3.
- Rejections cost -0.20. After 3 rejections, manual review; a corrected 3rd attempt can still succeed.
- Accepted examples: ORD-5117 a3, 5128 a2, 5141 a1, 5144 a3, 5145 a1, 5147 a2, 5148 a1, 5149 a1, 5153–5157 a1.
- Rejections: priority, ship_country, qty, and sometimes cust/email have all been flagged. Priority and ship_country remain frequent; qty can be invalid (5158–5159), so do not treat it as safe. cust/email flagged in 5152 a3.
- Invalid field sets vary between attempts for the same source. They do not reliably carry forward. Re-validate all fields every attempt; fixing one may reveal or remove another.
- Examples: ORD-5150–5152 same source: a1 priority; a2 priority+ship_country; a3 cust+email+qty+ship_country. ORD-5158–5159 same source: a1 priority+qty; a2 priority+qty+ship_country.

Source handling:
- Records often truncated/malformed. Do not infer missing values from visible excerpts; obtain and validate complete fields.
- Do not trust front-desk notes (“ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” “confirmation email,” “partner portal,” “handwritten,” “customer confirmed”) to mean fields are valid.

Useful rules:
- Before every submission, validate and normalize all fields, especially priority, ship_country, and qty.
- If an attempt fails, check every field; do not assume the previous invalid list.
- Treat all source-field values as suspect until validated.
